source_contract: Goal startup first reads thread, requires idle and persisted(non-ephemeral,path non-None), then reserves route before clearing old goal and activating turn routing.
Sets goal active and waits real goal start up to constant30s. On BaseException conditionally cancels (activated or not InvalidRequestError), then finishes/unregisters state.

Async goal startup is distinct from ordinary-turn startup: a daemon codex-goal-start worker completes a concurrent Future from sync.start_goal_operation; caller awaits asyncio.shield(asyncio.wrap_future(operation)).

On CancelledError, register cleanup_cancelled_start callback and immediately rethrow. If completed.result raises BaseException, callback returns. If result gives state, callback starts another daemon codex-goal-start-cleanup; it calls sync.cancel_goal_operation and in finally state.finish then sync.unregister_goal_operation.

No daemon join or cleanup completion ACK occurs before that CancelledError is returned. Actual scheduling, continued startup, callbacks, body outcomes and resource liveness remain NOT_RUN; do not infer no effect or stopped goal. Sync startup catch order also does not guarantee later cleanup if a preceding cleanup step itself raises BaseException.

Also cancel goal startup before versus after operation result, result failing versus succeeding, callback cleanup raising, and verify successful-result cleanup daemon finally finishes/unregisters even when cancel raises. Compare ordinary-turn cancellation callback (subscription close only) without claiming any schedule was observed.

source_contract: Cursor merges actual turns into one logical ID, emits first started only, suppresses goal status notifications and uses terminal goal/cleared/failed/interrupted state to decide logical completion.

cancel_goal_operation tries pause_goal(threadId) via thread/goal/set(status=paused); an ordinary Exception from pause is suppressed, then _interrupt_goal_operation is still called. This is not unconditional suppression of BaseException.

Interrupt selects current turn ID, else completed_turn.id, else started_turn.id; absent ID sends no interrupt. First turn_interrupt success ends; non-InvalidRequest Exception is suppressed without retry.

Only InvalidRequestError whose message starts with expected active turn id enters rollover recovery. Candidate is _active_turn_id_from_error(exc) OR state.current_turn() (extracted truthy ID takes precedence); absent or same ID sends no second request. Different candidate sends exactly one second turn_interrupt; its Exception is suppressed. At most two syntactic interrupt attempts per invocation, not a general retry loop.

These client-side IDs/error text and pause/interrupt requests do not grant native authority or prove remote stopped state, effect absence, terminal ACK or process exit. Normal goal close/aclose only finishes/unregisters; sync KeyboardInterrupt and async goal cancellation explicitly invoke this cancel policy; ordinary-turn cancellation remains different.

Include pause Exception followed by interrupt, absent/current/completed/started ID selection, first interrupt success, unrelated InvalidRequestError prefix, matching-prefix extracted different/same/absent ID, state.current_turn fallback, second interrupt failure, and no third attempt.

Dropping pause on goal cancel, skipping interrupt after ordinary pause Exception, retrying unrelated errors, using state fallback despite a truthy extracted same ID, retrying equal/absent IDs, or a third interrupt must be rejected.
